stories.headline: Update: India and Nepal sign 8 pacts; Modi offers NPR 24,000 crore aid package
stories.summary: After talks in New Delhi, India and Nepal signed eight agreements covering health, traditional medicine, a satellite communication network, training, urban development, research, and livestock and fisheries. Modi announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal's flood recovery, and the two leaders flagged off the weekly Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu-Kamala Express. They also laid foundation stones for the 669 MW Lower Arun hydro project and a Jhapa oil terminal, and opened phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhganj pipeline.
stories.why_it_matters: It is Shah's first bilateral visit abroad as PM, and it locks in Indian-backed power, fuel and rail links with Nepal.
stories.note: What changed: the talks ended with 8 signed agreements, an aid package and new projects.

image.alt: Narendra Modi shakes hands with Nepal PM Balendra Shah in front of Indian and Nepali flags

stories.headline: S&P Global sees India as Asia-Pacific's fastest-growing economy in 2027
stories.summary: S&P Global says India's economy can grow about 7% both this financial year and next (to March 2028), helped by strong goods exports, government-led investment, steady consumer spending and faster credit growth. It expects inflation to average 5.3% this year, with risks tilted higher, easing to 4.7% next year.
stories.why_it_matters: A 7% outlook from a major agency supports foreign investor interest in Indian assets.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (Hindi service), reporting S&P Global's Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 outlook.

impact.why: A steady 7% growth view supports confidence in India's economy.

stories.headline: RBI keeps SBI, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank on its 'too big to fail' list
stories.summary: The RBI's 2026 list of domestic systemically important banks again names State Bank of India, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. They must keep extra core capital of 0.80%, 0.40% and 0.20% of risk-weighted assets respectively, unchanged in bucket terms.

stories.headline: RBI issues final securitisation rules, effective from April 1, 2027
stories.summary: The RBI issued final amendments to its securitisation directions to make the issue and transfer of securitisation notes more efficient, liquid and transparent. They cover commercial banks, small finance banks, NBFCs and all-India financial institutions, and follow feedback on a July draft.

stories.headline: Iran vows 'all available means' against US blockade; Trump eyes strikes in new year
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday Iran will use all available means to counter the US naval blockade, which he called an act of military aggression. On Sunday, Trump told Fox News he is inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the New Year if talks fail, and said ships running the blockade would be sunk. Qatar-mediated talks remain stalled.
stories.why_it_matters: Rising war risk around Hormuz can quickly push oil higher, which hurts India's import bill and the rupee.
stories.note: Statements by each side; both are reported by several outlets.

image.alt: A container ship sails through the Gulf of Oman off Khor Fakkan, UAE

impact.why: Threats of new strikes and blockade clashes raise supply risk near Hormuz.

stories.headline: At least 15 killed as Russian strikes hit towns around Kyiv
stories.summary: Russian attacks killed at least 15 people in the Kyiv region, Ukrainian officials say. A strike on a five-storey building in Dymer killed at least 11, a supermarket strike in Vyshneve killed 3, and one person died in Bila Tserkva. Ukraine's drones hit oil storage sites in Russia's Tatarstan, Russian media say.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera (citing Reuters and AFP).

stories.headline: Rupee ends 5-day winning run, falls 30 paise to 92.92 per dollar
stories.summary: The rupee settled 30 paise weaker at 92.92 per dollar (provisional), after touching 93.11 during the day. Dealers blamed the sharp fall in Indian shares and dollar buying by importers, including two large conglomerates, Business Standard says. Dealers see a 92.70 to 93.30 range in the near term.
stories.why_it_matters: It ends a five-day rise just as Indian markets shut for a holiday on Tuesday.
stories.note: Business Standard puts the close at 92.91; PTI reports 92.92.

impact.why: Importer dollar demand and the stock sell-off pushed the rupee lower.

stories.headline: Dollar and US yields rise as traders price a 96% chance of a December Fed hike
stories.summary: The dollar index rose about 0.4% to near 104.3. US 10-year yields climbed about 3 basis points to near 4.94% and 2-year yields more than 5 points to 4.67%. CME FedWatch shows about a 96% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise in December, up from about 92% on Friday.
stories.why_it_matters: Higher US rates and a firm dollar make it harder for the rupee to gain.

impact.why: A near-certain Fed hike supports the dollar.
Short-term US yields rose on hike bets.

stories.headline: Wall Street jumps 4-6% as Nvidia soars about 30% on Huang's return as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after he resigned, saying US government officials told it he poses no national security risk. Nvidia shares rose about 30%. Soon after the open the S&P 500 was up about 4.9% at 7,246 and the Nasdaq about 6.9%, after both ended Friday in a correction; Micron, AMD and CoreWeave also jumped.
stories.why_it_matters: It is a sharp turn after Wall Street's worst week since 2020 and could lift Indian IT and tech when Indian markets reopen on Wednesday.
stories.note: Nvidia's independent review of Huang's conduct is still going on.

image.alt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a black leather jacket at an event

impact.why: The board brought back Huang as CEO, ending the leadership crisis.
AI and chip stocks led a broad rebound after a 10% correction.
A US tech rally usually lifts Indian IT exporters.

stories.headline: Sensex sinks 1,484 points, Nifty 1.75% in worst day in nine months
stories.summary: The Sensex fell 1,483.72 points (1.77%) to 82,435.99 and the Nifty 450.95 points (1.75%) to 25,349.65, ending a two-day rise. Nifty Metal fell about 3.6% and PSU and private bank indices over 3%; Tata Steel dropped about 8.5% after its APL Apollo deal, with Axis, HDFC and ICICI Bank down over 3%. Nifty IT rose about 2%. The US rally began only after Indian markets closed.
stories.why_it_matters: Indian markets are shut on Tuesday, so Wall Street's rebound will be priced in on Wednesday.

impact.why: Biggest one-day drop in nine months, led by banks and metals.
Shares fell about 8.5% after the APL Apollo stake deal.
IT stocks gained about 2% against the trend.

stories.headline: Update: Gold extends rebound to about $3,669, up over 4% on the day
stories.summary: US gold futures rose to about $3,669 an ounce by 8:35 PM IST, up about 4.4% from Friday's settle of $3,515.4 and above midday's $3,619, as the dollar's rally paused earlier and yields eased. Gold fell about 9% last week. In India, MCX gold rose back above Rs 1.25 lakh per 10 grams, reports say.
stories.note: What changed: gold rose further in the afternoon and evening.

impact.why: Bargain buying after last week's 9% fall.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal
stories.summary: CrowdStrike will buy rival Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing it at about $43.9 billion, giving 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share. CrowdStrike says the deal takes it into network security. Zscaler shares rose about 14% before the open and CrowdStrike fell about 8%.

impact.why: Shares fell on the cost of the all-stock deal.
Buyout at a premium lifted the stock.
